The trace covers six hops. The frontend UserAvatar component requests the avatar. The converter formats the URL. The handler serves GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar. getUserByUsername calls Store.GetUser. Store.GetUser calls driver.GetUser. The database layer is sqlite/mysql/postgres user.go. package v1

import (
	"fmt"
	"regexp"
	"time"

	"github.com/pkg/errors"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/timestamppb"

	v1pb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/api/v1"
	storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
)

func convertUserFromStore(user *store.User, viewer *store.User) *v1pb.User {
	userpb := &v1pb.User{
		Name:        BuildUserName(user.Username),
		State:       convertStateFromStore(user.RowStatus),
		CreateTime:  timestamppb.New(time.Unix(user.CreatedTs, 0)),
		UpdateTime:  timestamppb.New(time.Unix(user.UpdatedTs, 0)),
		Role:        convertUserRoleFromStore(user.Role),
		Username:    user.Username,
		DisplayName: user.Nickname,
		AvatarUrl:   user.AvatarURL,
		Description: user.Description,
	}
	if canViewerAccessUserEmail(viewer, user) {
		userpb.Email = user.Email
	}

Reading user_service_converters.go for avatar URL conversion, store/user.go for GetUser, and the SQLite GetUser implementation.

Also checking server.go for route registration.

I need to examine ListUsers in sqlite to find the SQL query for avatar_url.

GetUser calls ListUsers.

Reading the remainder of ListUsers in sqlite and BuildUserName to understand the full SQL and username construction. The avatar URL format is `/file/users/{username}/avatar`. The frontend receives this path from `convertUserFromStore`, then `UserAvatar` renders it as an `` source. This triggers a GET request to `/file/users/:identifier/avatar`. The route is registered in `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` and handled by `serveUserAvatar`. That function calls `getUserByUsername`, then `Store.GetUser` and `Store.ListUsers`, which execute `driver.ListUsers` and fetch the avatar from the database. `parseDataURI` decodes the base64 string, and `c.Blob` returns the image. The concrete file paths are now mapped out. The route registration lives in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. `store/user.go` contains `Store.GetUser` and `Store.ListUsers`. The SQLite driver implementation is in `store/db/sqlite/user.go`. The schema that defines the `avatar_url` column is in `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`. Authentication runs before the data hop. `getCurrentUser` and the authenticator check access rights first. External avatar URLs bypass the file server entirely; the browser fetches them directly. The traced path applies only to base64 avatars stored in the database.

message.text:
Enough information has been gathered to trace the full data path for a profile image request.

The trace begins at the browser request. The avatar URL originates in UserAvatar.tsx. The chain continues through fileserver.go: RegisterRoutes, serveUserAvatar, getUserByUsername, and finally Store.GetUser in store/user.go.

Store.ListUsers in store/user.go queries the SQLite user table via DB.ListUsers in store/db/sqlite/user.go. The avatar_url column is defined in store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql. The code decodes the base64 data URI from user.AvatarURL. On private instances, getCurrentUser may authenticate the request before reaching the handler.

The response returns from the data layer through parseDataURI on user.AvatarURL, then c.Blob in fileserver.go.

h07. **Serving handler:** `serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` The browser loads another user’s avatar via `` (`web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx`). That URL is set when user records are converted for the API: base64 avatars become `/file/{name}/avatar` (i.e. `/file/users/{username}/avatar`) in `convertUserFromStore` — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go`. Hop chain from HTTP request to stored data: ``` RegisterRoutes (GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go Store.GetUser — store/user.go Store.ListUsers — store/user.go DB.ListUsers — store/db/sqlite/user.go (also store/db/mysql/user.go, store/db/postgres/user.go) SQL SELECT … avatar_url … FROM user — store/db/sqlite/user.go user.avatar_url column — store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql ``` After the row is read, `serveUserAvatar` decodes the stored base64 data URI via `parseDataURI` and returns the bytes with `c.Blob` — both in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. On a private instance (no public `instance_url`), `serveUserAvatar` first calls `getCurrentUser` → `authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`, `server/auth/authenticator.go`) before loading the user row. Route registration at startup: `fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)` — `server/server.go`.
